description:
Cost comparison of human labour (or a human service) against robot options (buy, lease, robots-as-a-service, robot service provider) for one of 22 jobs in one of 8 countries (US, DE, GB, JP, CN, IN, BR, MX). Uses the same model as whirrwork.com/tools/robot-vs-human/: every default input has a source or is flagged as an assumption (see input_sources). Returns monthly/annual cost, cost per unit, payback months, break-even utilisation, 5-year NPV vs the baseline, a verdict, non-cost factors, sensitivity ranking, and projections to 2035 with a crossover year range (robots-fast, base, robots-slow). Projections are modelled estimates, not facts: say so, and quote the range rather than one year.
Examples: {"job":"warehouse-picking","country":"US"}; {"job":"commercial-floor-cleaning","country":"DE","inputs":{"volume":60000}}; {"job":"machine-tending","country":"US","region":"US-TX","include_projections":false}.

baseline.description: Which human option to compare against (e.g. "human" or "service"). Defaults to the job default.

country.description: Country for wage, on-cost and currency defaults (sourced: BLS, ILOSTAT, MHLW, NBS, Eurostat).

include_projections.description: Include 2026-2035 projections for three scenarios and the crossover year range.

include_tornado.description: Include the sensitivity (tornado) ranking of inputs by NPV swing.

inputs.description: Optional overrides of default inputs, in the country currency. Fractions as 0-1 (uptime 0.85, rate 0.08).

job.description: Job slug. One of the 22 jobs in GET /api/v1/robot-vs-human/jobs.

region.description: Optional regional wage preset: US states US-CA, US-TX, US-NY, US-FL, US-IL, US-WA, US-PA, US-OH; China CN-E, CN-C, CN-W, CN-NE.

name: compare_robot_vs_human

input_sources.description: Per input: status (sourced | derived | converted | assumption | user), source_id, source_url, note

inputs.description: Resolved inputs actually used (defaults + overrides), in the country currency; fractions 0-1

breakeven_utilisation.description: Share of available hours a robot must work to break even; >1 = unreachable

payback_months.description: null = never pays back (or this is the baseline)

projections.description: Per scenario (slow, base, fast): yearly cost per unit 2026-2035, constant 2026 money

title: Robot or human? Compare the cost
